package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware targeting Linux VoIP systems, not a package manager ecosystem)
package_info.why_malicious: CDRThief is a malware specifically designed to target Linux VoIP systems from the Chinese company Linknat. It steals sensitive call-records and database information, including credentials and IP addresses, indicating clear data theft and espionage intent.

execution_context.file_location: VoIP system process (likely a malicious shared object or binary injected into the Linknat system)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malware reads call-records and database files, extracts credentials and IP addresses, and exfiltrates them to an external server.
malicious_snippets.code_language: C/C++ (typical for Linux malware, though exact language not specified)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code accesses call-record and database files, extracts credentials and IP addresses, and sends this data to a remote command-and-control server, resulting in sensitive information exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing and exfiltrating call-records, credentials, and IP addresses is not a normal operation for VoIP system binaries and indicates data theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate VoIP system processes should not transmit sensitive database contents or credentials to external servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: VoIP systems may legitimately access call-records and database files for internal processing or backup, but never for exfiltration to unknown external servers.
key_indicators: Unauthorized access to sensitive database files
Exfiltration of credentials and IP addresses
Network communication to external, attacker-controlled servers

attack_chain.action: Malware is deployed onto the target Linknat Linux VoIP system (initial infection vector unknown).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware execution within the VoIP system process

attack_chain.action: Malware executes and accesses call-records and database files, extracting credentials and IP addresses.
Extracted data is sent to an external command-and-control server controlled by the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive information from the compromised VoIP system

behavioral_signatures: Unusual access to VoIP system call-records and database files
Extraction and aggregation of credentials and IP addresses
Outbound network connections to unknown or suspicious external servers from VoIP system processes
file_indicators: Unexpected binaries or shared objects within Linknat VoIP system directories
Unusual file access patterns to call-record or database files
network_indicators: Outbound connections from VoIP system to external IPs/domains not associated with legitimate Linknat operations
Data exfiltration patterns (large or frequent data uploads) from VoIP system processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor VoIP system processes for unauthorized access to call-records and database files, and alert on any outbound network connections to unknown external servers. Correlate file access logs with network activity to identify potential data exfiltration. Use file integrity monitoring to detect new or modified binaries in VoIP system directories.
